notes.1: Makes 6 biscuits and about 3 cups of gravy.
notes.2: Makes 12 biscuits and about 6 cups of gravy. They fit on one sheet pan, 3 rows of 4.

move.title: Biscuits from the oven, gravy from the pan
move.body: Biscuits and gravy is a Southern breakfast: flaky buttermilk biscuits split open and smothered in a creamy, peppery gravy. Today you'll bake a batch of biscuits and, while they bake, brown turkey sausage and thicken milk into gravy with a roux, so both are ready together.

callback.body: You've made these biscuits before. This time they bake while you make the gravy, so the two finish at the same time.

why.title: Cold butter, tall biscuits
why.body: Frozen butter grated into the flour turns to steam in a hot oven and puffs the biscuits into layers.

why.title: A roux in the sausage pan
why.body: Flour stirred into the sausage and butter for 2 minutes cooks out its raw taste. Milk whisked in slowly turns it into a smooth gravy.

why.title: It thickens as it simmers
why.body: Flour thickens milk only once it's close to a boil. Keep the gravy at a gentle simmer for a few minutes and it goes from thin to creamy. It thickens more as it sits.

wrong.fix: The milk went in too fast. Whisk hard; the lumps break up as it simmers.
Whisk in a splash of milk.
Simmer 2 more minutes. It thickens as it cooks and as it sits.
The butter was too warm. Freeze it longer next time.

choices: A roux: flour cooked in the fat

quiz.q: Why is the milk whisked in slowly?
quiz.explain: A little at a time, whisking.

quiz.q: What temperature does turkey sausage need?

steps.text: Put the biscuits' butter in the freezer.
steps.tip: Heat the oven and measure everything while it chills.

steps.text: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 450°F. Line the sheet pan with parchment.
Whisk the biscuits' flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar in the large bowl.
Grate the frozen butter on the large holes of the box grater into the flour, and toss with the fork.
Stir in the buttermilk with the fork just until there's no dry flour.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. Raw flour can make you sick.

steps.text: Pat the dough 1 inch thick on a floured counter, fold it in thirds, and pat it out again. Do this 3 times, then cut 6 biscuits straight down and set them on the pan, sides touching.
Bake the biscuits until tall and golden. Start the gravy now.
Cook the sausage in the skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink is left.
Throw away the package and wash your hands with soap.
Check a pile of sausage with the thermometer: 165°F.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the gravy's butter, let it melt, then sprinkle in the flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the milk. Simmer, stirring, until the gravy is thick and creamy. Stir in the pepper and salt.
steps.look: Thick enough to coat the back of the spoon.

steps.text: With oven mitts, take out the biscuits. Turn off the oven and the stove. Split the biscuits and ladle the gravy over them.

substitutions.note: Use bulk turkey breakfast sausage and leave out the sausage seasonings.

freeze-butter.text: Put the biscuits' butter in the freezer.

sausage.text: Brown the beef in the skillet over medium-high heat, sprinkling in the seasoning and breaking it into small crumbles.

wash-sausage.text: Discard the package and wash your hands.

check-sausage.text: Check a pile of sausage: at least 165°F. Turn the heat to low.

oven.text: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan.

dry.text: Weigh {qty:flour-ap} of flour into the large bowl and whisk in the baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar.

grate.text: Grate the frozen butter into the flour and toss.

wet.text: Stir in the buttermilk just until no dry flour remains.

fold.text: Pat 1 inch thick, letter-fold three times, and cut the biscuits straight down. Set them on the pan, sides touching.

bake.text: Bake the biscuits. Start the roux as they go in.

roux.text: Turn the sausage to medium, add the gravy's butter, then the flour, and stir 2 minutes.

milk.text: Whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer until it coats a spoon. Season with the pepper and salt.
milk.tip: Too thick by the time the biscuits are done? Whisk in a splash of milk.

serve.text: Pull the biscuits, turn everything off, split them, and ladle the gravy over.

add.text: Mix the sausage's salt, pepper, thyme, chili flakes, garlic powder, and brown sugar in the small bowl.

move.title: Scaled by weight, timed to the minute
move.body: This week's skill is scaling a quick bread and timing it to the main. Pick the size you're feeding (12 doubles it), and the amounts here scale by weight. You'll season ground beef into breakfast sausage yourself and run the gravy on a timeline so it's thick and hot the minute the biscuits come out.

quiz.q: Doubling the biscuits, what happens to the baking time?
choices: It stays the same, since each biscuit is the same size
Doubling cups doubles the measuring error too

quiz.q: Which part can wait: biscuits or gravy?
quiz.explain: Biscuits go flat as they sit.

quiz.q: What does the gravy's roux do?

add.title: Scale by weight
add.body: Doubling cups adds the error twice. Weighed flour doubles exactly, and the leaveners double with it. The baking time stays the same: each biscuit is the same size.

add.title: Work back from the oven
add.body: The biscuits need 13 minutes in the oven and won't wait. The gravy holds. So the sausage is browned before the biscuits go in, and the gravy simmers while they bake.
